To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ER‐resident TRP protein TRPP2 protects cells from apoptosis, and that the loss of TRPP function is a cause for increased apoptosis in polycystic kidneys.
the ER Ca2+-permeable TRPP2 channel protects cells from apoptosis.
the TRPP2 channels in the endoplamic reticulum (a sub‐organelle within cells) protect cells against apoptosis by lowering the calcium ion concentration inside the endoplasmatic reticulum.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of intracellular TRPP2 channels in the regulation of ER Ca2+ homeostasis and apoptosis, which is important for understanding the function of TRP channels in the ER and for understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms of ADPKD.
the role of TRPP2, an ion channel mutated in the most frequent monogenic kidney disease, in apoptosis.
the role of intracellular Ca(2+) signalling in the regulation of cell death.
